verdict: Round 4 is untouched, the round-5 page entries are consistent with screen.json and prompts5.json, and almost every number in RESULTS5.md reproduced. Three things are not clean: the test suite of the tools has one failing test (introduced when the select step added two hand skips), shield_bright_2 s11 leaves the page 4.0 dB under its two family mates, and the first valve pick ends hard (its last 50 ms are 16.7 dB under its maximum, inside the 20 dB of point 4). The README round-5 section has wrong counts and tells the reader to generate Stable Audio against the owner's MOSS-only decision. The generation redo was bit-identical for 3 of 4 files; one MOSS file differs at about -79 dB. Nobody listened; nothing here says how anything sounds.

Carried round-4 skips: shield_3 s16 9.5 % above 60 Hz is a plain README fault (reproduced from record: 0.0949); thruster_1 s16 'silence inside the cut' is a README fault, not re-measured. Kept inconsistency: thruster_bang_1 s11 (picked, ev5_4_thruster_bang_2) has a flat plateau 19 to 25 dB under its 0.2 s bang for the remaining 1 s while bang_1 s12 was skipped for a similar run-up at -15 to -22 dB.

mustFix: tools/sound/tests/test_screen.py line 1012: the assertion 'skips5.json skips == []' fails now that skips5.json holds the two round-5 hand skips (43 tests, 1 failed). Change the assertion to check what the test is about (the file exists, is a list), then re-run: the suite must be 43 of 43.

ev5_6_shield_bright_2_moss_p2s11 leaves the page 4.0 dB under its two family mates (-28.05 against -24.05 and -24.07) because the true-peak ceiling stopped the gain (crest 35.0 dB). An unequal level biases a listening comparison. Replace it before the owner listens (kept shield_bright candidates with a lower crest exist, for example shield_bright_1 s12 or s13 at 92 % and 91 % above 60 Hz, if they pass the same checks) or state the miss on the page; the orchestrator decides.

ev5_3_thruster_valve_1_moss_r4p1s12 ends within 20 dB of its maximum in the last 50 ms of the published file (16.7 dB; 14.2 dB on the raw cut). screen.py's cut-off test does not see it because the raw file drops at 1.004 s. Either accept it explicitly as a hard-ending burst (RESULTS5 already says hard end) or re-cut/skip it; at present point 4 of the brief is not met for this pick.
